title: Top 10 Essential Verbs in English for Absolute Beginners (A0–A1)
dek: Master the 10 most high-frequency verbs in English with A0–A1 adapted conjugations, collocations, false-friend warnings, and a 14-language comparative matrix.

blocks.text: Welcome to the essential guide to high-frequency English verbs for absolute beginners (A0–A1)! Mastering these core verbs will unlock over 80% of daily conversations.

items: **1. To Be (am / is / are):** Identity, states, and locations (*I am a student*, *He is at home*, *They are ready*).
**2. To Have (have / has):** Possession and relationships (*I have a book*, *She has a sister*). Note: Age uses *to be* (*I am 20 years old*).
**3. To Do / To Make:** Actions and creation (*Do homework*, *Do laundry* vs. *Make coffee*, *Make dinner*).
**4. To Go (go / goes):** Movement away from speaker (*I go to school*, *She goes home*).
**5. To Come (come / comes):** Movement toward speaker (*Come here*, *They come from France*).
**6. To Say / To Tell:** Speech and communication (*Say hello*, *Say yes* vs. *Tell a story*, *Tell me*).
**7. To See / To Look:** Visual perception (*I see a bird* vs. *Look at the map*).
**8. To Know:** Factual knowledge and familiarity (*I know the answer*, *Do you know John?*).
**9. To Want:** Expressing desire (*I want water*, *She wants to learn*).
**10. To Like:** Expressing preference (*I like tea*, *They like soccer*).

• **Indo-European:** Features tense auxiliary verbs and person/number inflections.
• **Turkic Family (Tatar, Bashkir, Chuvash):** Agglutinative suffix structures expressing tense and person without separate helper verbs.
• **Kartvelian (Georgian):** Polypersonal verb agreement marking subject and indirect/direct objects.
